title: Member Disclosure: Credit for a Good-Faith Interest Payment Within the Grace Period — Farm Real Estate Loans
content:
On a Farm Real Estate Loans installment, a good-faith interest payment within the grace period earns a credit taken off the late-charge percentage, the amount counted being the interest paid on the installment when the most recent interest payment was received within the grace period: when that amount is more than half of the installment, the credit is 1.0 percentage point; when it is half of the installment or less, the credit is 0.5 percentage point; when no interest payment was received within the grace period, there is no credit. The late-charge percentage left after credits is never below zero.

**Terms.**

- *The grace period* runs from the due date (day 0) through the last grace day; the most recent interest payment on the loan must have been received on or before that day.
- *The interest paid on the installment* is the total of the interest payments that point to that installment's bill.
- *Half of the installment* is half of the installment amount.

| Product | Grace period (calendar days) |
|---|---|
| FarmLand Variable-Rate Mortgage | 15 |
| FarmLand 3-Year Adjustable Mortgage | 15 |
| FarmLand 5-Year Adjustable Mortgage | 15 |
| FarmLand 10-Year Adjustable Mortgage | 15 |
| FarmLand 15-Year Fixed Mortgage | 15 |
| FarmLand 25-Year Fixed Mortgage | 15 |

## Credit ladder (hypothetical installment of USD 12000.00)

| Most recent interest payment received | Interest paid on the installment | Credit (percentage points) |
|---|---|---|
| day 12 | 6000.01 (more than half) | 1.0 |
| day 12 | 6000.00 (exactly half) | 0.5 |
| day 15 (last grace day) | 2500.00 | 0.5 |
| day 16 | 2500.00 | none |
| no interest payment | — | none |
